subject: Hierarchical multivariate continuous time state space - can INLA work for me?

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Hierarchical multivariate continuous time state space - can INLA work for me?
parts:
I have had some difficulty working out whether the INLA approach may be useful for me, I suspect it can but any help would be wonderful...

I have a hierarchical multivariate state space model, currently setup in Stan. latent states are integrated over with a continuous-discrete filter, so p(y_i) (data for one subject) depends only on phi_i, a vector containing subject specific parameters. The following is all vectors except the sigmacholesky matrix:

phi_i = f(mu+x_i * sigmacholesky)    , x_i~N(0,1)
mu=g(theta1) ,   theta1 ~ N(0,1)
sigmacholesky=h(theta2,theta3) ,   theta2~ N(0,1) (log std deviations) ,    theta3~ N(0,1)   (logit link + linear scale of partial correlations)


Can this work, would it need to be structured differently, or is there no possibility? If it can be made to work reasonably, hopefully by integrating to an R function returning the likelihood for given values, I would like to include it as a possibility for the ctsem software I've written to specify and fit such models... cheers for any thoughts.

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hierarchical multivariate continuous time state space - can INLA work for me?
parts:
As far as I can tell, that won't work in inla, which only works on models of the form 

Y_i ~ pi(y | x_i, tau)

x_i = A*x
x ~ N(0,Q(theta)^{-1})

tau,theta low dimensional with no restriction on their distributions. 

Here x is a vector and A is a known matrix. 

Best wishes 

Dan
